surface_source.quote: Add Grok tmux session, whole-file source viewer, and +/− member marks.

agents.quote: However, I just had grok build me a script editor.  It took it 30 minutes.

also.quote: I had @grok implement this from a single prompt. It took 40 minutes.

history.quote: grok-cli did a splendid job of modifying my app to convert synchronous http/get calls in the drawing loop into an asynchronous process.
I am impressed that it has a much better grasp of the code than grok.

history.value: Claude as architect, Codex as coder and reviewer
history.quote: I found that the best agent to use as the architect was Claude.
I just cancelled my Claude account.  I've been using codex, and haven't used Claude in several weeks.

agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: I'm using codex to review the code that grok wrote.  Good results.

models.name: Grok
models.quote: It is eerie just how good @grok is now.  I've stopped using any other model for the time being.

history.quote: After one day of using Claude (Yes, I heard all of you out there in the peanut gallery) I am both impressed and horrified.

review_style.value: Does not read agent code: Codex reviews Grok's output, he inspects a UML diagram colored by CRAP and mutation scores
review_style.quote: People seem shocked that the author of Clean Code doesn't read code anymore.

also.quote: I'm using codex to review the code that grok wrote.  Good results.
A simple demo of uml-viewer.  This is how I review the projects I create with agents nowadays.

My current strategy is to not read any of the code written by my agents. That’s the only way I can take advantage of their productivity. What I do instead is to surround the agents with extreme constraints.

harness.value: A few agents on isolated tasks, prompted by hand to run crap, dry and mutate; no harness
harness.quote: I'm back to working the way I did in March.  A few agents open doing isolated tasks.  Manually prompting them to do crap, dry, and mutate.  No harness.

history.value: swarm-forge: role agents (specifier, coder, cleaner, architect, hardener, QA) in tmux and git worktrees
history.quote: I just ran a swarm-forge (branch six-pack) with six agents.  Specifier, coder, cleaner, architect, hardender, QA.
And while I was heads-down getting that to work, the agents got a LOT better.  So much so that when I came up for air, the need for my harness was obviated.

rules_files.quote: Do not commit or push unless asked. Esc interrupts a turn in this terminal;

signature.caption: colored by CRAP + mutation
signature.why: Our pick: instead of reading agent code, he drills through a live UML diagram of the system, colored by CRAP and mutation scores, and tells a companion agent what to change.
signature.quote: The tool displays the structure of the system in a UML-like diagram, color coded with crap and mutation scores.

archetype.why: Has agents build his own quality tools (crapper, mutator, dryer, uml-viewer) and supervises through them instead of reading code.

signature_quote.value: People seem shocked that the author of Clean Code doesn't read code anymore.
signature_quote.more: But that should not be surprising.
